facts.value: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion that prescribes a path of non-violence, truth and anekantavada for all forms of living beings in this universe.
The goal is to eliminate all the Karmas and hence to attain freedom from the cycle of birth and death (saṃsāra), achieving nirvana.
Jains are found mostly in India.
Historians date the Mahavira as about contemporaneous with the Buddha in the 5th-century BCE, and the historical Parshvanatha is placed in 8th or 7th century BCE.
Digambara Jainism (or sky-clad) is mainly practiced in South India.
Their holy books are Pravachanasara and Samayasara written by their Prophets Kundakunda and Amritchandra.
Shwetambara Jainism (or white-clad) is mainly practiced in Western India.
Their holy books are Jain Agamas, written by their Prophet Sthulibhadra.
